svg.title: Stationarity vs Nonstationarity (Unit Root)
svg.desc: In a stationary series shocks decay and moments are fixed; with a unit root shocks accumulate, variance diverges and standard regression distributions break down.
svg.text: A series where shocks fade vs one where shocks accumulate forever
t and F statistics behave normally
Model the level as it is
Variance grows in proportion to t
Log prices and exchange rate levels
Whatever the shock, it comes back to the same level
Paths drift apart and variance grows
Same starting point, yet anywhere is possible later
Both tests point to a unit root
Stationary series let shocks decay with fixed moments; a unit root lets shocks accumulate forever.
That difference breaks standard regression distributions and produces spurious results.
Failing to reject the null is
